title: Stoichiometry and Reactions - Chemistry - Mole Concept
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following values represents Avogadro's number?
questions.explain: Avogadro's number is the number of constituent particles (usually atoms or molecules) that are contained in one mole of a given substance, defined as exactly $6.02214076 \times 10^{23}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How many moles of Carbon (C) are present in $2.50 \times 10^{24}$ atoms of Carbon?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the mass of 0.500 moles of Calcium (Ca)? (Atomic mass of Ca = 40.08 g/mol)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which sample contains the greatest number of atoms?
questions.explain: 1 mole of Ar contains $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ atoms. 1 mole of H$_2$ contains $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ *molecules*, but since each molecule has 2 atoms, it contains $1.2 \times 10^{24}$ atoms. This is greater than the other options.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Calculate the number of molecules in 36.0 grams of water (H$_2$O). (Molar mass of H$_2$O = 18.02 g/mol)
questions.explain: First find moles: $\frac{36.0 \text{ g}}{18.02 \text{ g/mol}} \approx 2.0 \text{ mol}$. Then multiply by Avogadro's number: $2.0 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 1.204 \times 10^{24}$ molecules.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: If a sample contains $3.01 \times 10^{23}$ molecules of CO$_2$, what is the mass of the sample? (Molar mass CO$_2$ = 44.01 g/mol)
questions.explain: $3.01 \times 10^{23}$ is exactly 0.5 moles. Mass = $0.5 \text{ mol} \times 44.01 \text{ g/mol} = 22.0 \text{ g}$.
